narration.text: Why 690,000 dead whales feed the deep sea.
A dead whale sinks below 1,000 metres.
It passes through four stages of feeding communities.
On average, they lie about 12 kilometres apart.
Scavengers strip flesh; worms and microbes feast on bones.
Some species may live almost nowhere else.
So a single whale becomes a deep-sea ecosystem.
